correctness.rationale: The partials force x1=0, then x4=x3=x2, then x2=x5=0, even over the algebraic closure. An independent point-pair calculation uses the unique leading-1 representatives of all 341 projective points over F4 and gets 81 points on X. Each pair determines a five-point line; a line occurs in ten pairs of cubic points exactly when all its five points lie on X. A nonzero restricted binary cubic has at most three projective zeros. The eight resulting lines equal the eight explicit equations, with graph 2K3+2K1 and four Frobenius transpositions. Exact subspace enumeration also reproduces the list from 5797 two-spaces. Intersections checked over F4 suffice geometrically since matrix rank does not change after extension. Substitution into the cubic gives the stated three distinct linear factors on each plane. Any three distinct coplanar lines form a graph triangle and any two of its sides span the plane, so no other split section is possible. The two planes meet only at [0:0:1:0:0], outside X, and descent would require a Frobenius-fixed line, of which there are none.
